institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Department of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Clinical Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 24, No. 1: percentage sensitivity, January to December 2017. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published July 2018.
reporting: Percent susceptible by specimen (blood, urine, pus wound swab, body fluids, respiratory isolates), organism (Gram-positive and Gram-negative tables) and location (OPD, ward, ICU), with the number of isolates per row; organism counts per specimen and location in bar charts with printed data labels and an "others" list.
method: MIC testing on Vitek 2, interpreted with CLSI 2017 guidelines; repeat isolates excluded (printed in parentheses).

verification.note: All 10 susceptibility tables (GPC and GNB, pages 2 to 6) were parsed from the PDF text layer (sgrhgrid2.py: pdfplumber word positions; column headers rebuilt from the rotated header text, the blood GPC "Glycopeptides" header, whose last letter the text layer lost, read from the image; OPD, ward and ICU taken from each row's background colour and checked against the row order; organism labels assigned to each triple of rows by vertical position), then every cell and every row n was compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 4 and cropped into left and right halves: no differences; the cells the validator does not keep were re-read. Organism bar charts: bar data labels were matched to the legend by legend order and swatch colour (barcounts.py) and the "others" lists parsed from the text layer inside each panel's box; every panel was checked arithmetically (legend counts plus Others equal the printed Isolates, the "others" list sums to Others, the bar values equal the text-layer data labels) and every panel was compared by eye with the chart rendered at scale 3.2; every recorded row n equals its chart count. Read from the image because the bar parse found no bars: the urine OPD legend (14 bars, E. coli 745 to Trichosporon asahii 10, Others 27) and the three body fluid legends (OPD Klebseilla spp. 11, E. coli 10, Others 40; ward Klebseilla spp. 27, E. coli 23, Enterococci spp. 14, Staphylococci spp. 10, Others 35; ICU Klebseilla spp. 22, Enterococci spp. 17, E. coli 16, Others 29); all balance and match the text-layer labels. Second reader 2026-09-26: see issues.

notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Volume 24, No. 1 (published July 2018), data January to December 2017, 8 pages; the bar-chart layout used in the 2024 file. Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus wound swab; body fluids; respiratory isolates): organism bar charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates, bars with printed data labels and a colour legend, and an "others" list) and Gram-positive (GPC) and Gram-negative (GNB) percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus (printed "Pus wound swab"), sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory (printed "Respiratory isolates"). Rows printed "Staphylococci spp." are separate from Staph. aureus and are recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci, as the 2011 edition labels the same row "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)"; enterococci ("Enterococci spp.", urine "Enterococcus spp."), Klebsiella and Acinetobacter are reported at genus level. Table sets differ from 2016: the blood GNB table has no Enterobacter rows, the urine GNB table no Acinetobacter rows, the urine GPC table adds Staph. aureus rows, and the body fluid GNB table has only E. coli and Klebsiella. Combined columns: "Cefoxitin/ Oxacillin" (every GPC table) is recorded under oxacillin, "Imipenem / Meropenem" (every GNB table) under meropenem, and "Glycopeptides" (every GPC table) under vancomycin; each such cell says so in its note. The blood S. pneumoniae rows print 100 in the Cefoxitin/Oxacillin column in all three settings; recorded under oxacillin as printed, with a cell note (the source does not say which test this is). The "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded; blood Salmonella also print chloramphenicol (recorded; no nalidixic acid column this year). Colistin (every GNB table) and tigecycline are printed as percent susceptible for Enterobacterales and non-fermenters; no interpretive criteria are stated for them beyond the CLSI 2017 note line. Isolate numbers: every recorded row n equals its organism's chart count; there are no chart and table mismatches on recorded rows. One row printed all "-" (not recorded) disagrees with the chart: blood ICU Salmonella paratyphi A (table n=0, ICU "others" list "Salmonella paratyphi A-1"). No percentage fails the whole-number check against its row n. Organism counts: every legend and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings and variants mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla spp." and "Klebseilla" as Klebsiella spp., "Serratia marscecens" (also "Serratia marscecens spp."), "Morganii spp." as Morganella, "Elizebethkingia meningoseptica", "S.tenotrophomonas maltophilia" and the two-line legend "Stenotrophomonas" / "maltophilia" as S. maltophilia, "L.monocytogenes", "Staphylococci spp." and "Staphylococci" as coagulase-negative staphylococci, "Enterococci spp." as Enterococcus spp.); entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. Blood ICU prints both "Salmonella entertidis-1" and "Salmonella typhimurium-1"; both are recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella as printed (the build adds counts of the same organism). "Salmonella entertidis" and "Salmonella typhimurium" are recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella. Fungal entries are not recorded as counts: most fungi on these charts are one "Fungal isolates" bar with no species, so the few species named in the "others" lists (urine OPD Trichosporon asahii 10; Aspergillus flavus, A. fumigatus and A. niger in pus, body fluid and respiratory panels, respiratory ICU A. flavus 27 and A. fumigatus 24; Candida albicans and C. tropicalis in respiratory OPD and ward) would understate them; they are listed in excluded; their susceptibility data were to be published separately in the next issue. Page 1 (Nocardia farcinica brain abscess case report), page 7 (prescription auditing of antimicrobials and drug resistance index trends) and page 8 (case report continued, references, CME and workshops, publications, award, book chapters, reflections, highlights based on blood isolates IPD, faculty) are not susceptibility tables. The PDF has no direct link: sgrh.com serves it only by an HTTP POST from the Microbiology Newsletter selector on https://sgrh.com/en/publications (issue "July-2018"; the server names the file mb-july2018.pdf); the downloaded file opens completely (8 pages).
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 987 cells, all 99 row n values and all 250 organism counts checked against the PDF: the seeded 25% sample of 247 cells from sample_cells.py (drawn from all 10 GPC and GNB tables on pages 2 to 6) was read blind from the page images (tables at scale 3 cut into halves with the row labels and n kept; small tables at scale 2 to 3) before comparing with the extraction, and every cell, every row n, every row's fill colour and every row label was also compared with an independent parse of the text layer written for this check (cell rectangles by fill colour, values centred in each cell, rotated header text per column, labels by vertical position).

Result: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected (sample 0 of 247; whole file 0 of 987 cells, 0 of 99 n, 0 of 250 counts). OPD, ward and ICU correct on every row (the CMYK row fills are the yellow, blue and pink of the colour key, always in OPD, ward, ICU order); the organism label of every row triple is correct (including the changed table sets: no blood Enterobacter, no urine Acinetobacter, urine Staph. aureus added, body fluid GNB E. coli and Klebsiella only); every printed value of a recorded column is in the file; the 15 printed rows not recorded are exactly the 15 rows printed all "-", as excluded says. No table reached the 2% threshold.

Column headers: Cefoxitin/ Oxacillin (every GPC table, 19 cells) under oxacillin, Glycopeptides (every GPC table, 31 cells; the blood GPC header reads "Glycopeptides" on the image) under vancomycin, Imipenem / Meropenem (57 cells) under meropenem and High Dose Gentamicin (7 cells) under gentamicin_hl match the printed headers, each with its note. The blood Strept. pneumoniae rows print 100 in the Cefoxitin/ Oxacillin column (4th column, between Ampicillin "-" and Ceftriaxone 100) in OPD, ward and ICU: confirmed on the page and correctly recorded under oxacillin with its note. The note line on pages 2 to 6 reads 2017 CLSI guidelines; this edition has no asterisk footnotes.

Charts: all 15 panels re-read from the images and the text layer; every panel balances and every bar pairs with its legend swatch in column order; every entry agrees with counts or excluded. The fungal species with canonical keys (urine OPD Trichosporon asahii 10; respiratory ICU Aspergillus flavus 27 and A. fumigatus 24; the Aspergillus and Candida "others" entries) are printed as listed in excluded; leaving them out of counts is the extraction's documented choice, not a reading error. Blood ICU Salmonella paratyphi A (table n=0 against "others" 1) is as printed. Every recorded row n equals its chart count.

Cells not kept: the 3 intrinsic cells (blood Acinetobacter aztreonam 67 OPD, 25 ward, 14 ICU) are printed that way; there are no caution cells. The page 7 and page 8 figures quoted in excluded match the pages, including the page 8 denominators (28 S. aureus, 60 enterococci, 243 Enterobacteriaceae).
